AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 21, 2020
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE
PROVISIONS OF THE GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-25-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC AND TELECONFERENCED. TO PARTICIPATE IN A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN
EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR CALL (562) 929-5720 BEFORE 5 P.M. ON MEETING DAY
TO REQUEST A CALL DURING THE MEETING FOR A SPECIFIC ITEM OR ORAL COMMUNICATIONS.
DETAILS ARE AVAILABLE ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393, which is also where the meeting may be viewed.
  6:15 PM
  VIA TELECONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957 –
  Consultation with the City Manager, City Attorney, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: APN 8056-017-901; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the
  City and Penny Reeves, Norwalk Auto Auction; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Jim Parker
  Executive Director of Regional Transportation

FLAG SALUTE
  John Ramirez
  Director of Community Development

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize April 25, 2020 as Arbor Day in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS
  COVID-19 Update.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of April 7
  and 14, 2020. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period March 8, 2020 – March
  21, 2020, in the total amount of $936,059.11. 630
   Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April
  1, 2020 - April 15, 2020, in the total amount of $1,336,692.59. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Moises
  Rodriguez. 830-18

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – APRIL 6, 2020 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-24 - FACSIMILE SIGNATURES – Staff recommends City Council adopt
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-24, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING CERTAIN BANKS TO HONOR ALL CHECKS, DRAFTS, AND
  WARRANTS WHEN BEARING CERTAIN SIGNATURES AND FACSIMILE SIGNATURES OF CITY
  OFFICIALS AS DESIGNATED AND RESCINDING ALL CONFLICTING RESOLUTIONS.

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT - BODY REPAIR AND PAINTING SERVICES FOR TRANSIT BUSES AND HEAVY
  DUTY VEHICLES - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with ABC Bus, Inc. for body
  repair and painting for Transit buses and heavy duty vehicles for a three (3) year term from July1, 2020
  through June 30, 2023, with an option to extend the agreement for two (2) one-year periods for a total
  contract value of $325,000; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  8.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Councilmembers either re-appoint current Advisory
  Body members or make new appointments for two-year terms beginning April 1, 2020 through March
  31, 2022. 200

  Report

  9.  APPOINTMENTS TO VARIOUS AGENCIES - Staff recommends City Council confirm the nominations
  as presented.

  Report

  10. RESOLUTION NO. 20-25 - APPOINTMENT TO THE CITY SELECTION COMMITTEE AND
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-26 – APPOINTMENT TO THE SANITATION DISTRICT NOS. 2 & 18 – Staff
  recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 20-25, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  DESIGNATING MAYOR JENNIFER PEREZ AS THE CITY’S REPRESENTATIVE AND VICE
  MAYOR TONY AYALA AS THE ALTERNATE FOR THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY CITY
  SELECTION COMMITTEE/EASTERN REGION; and

  b.  Resolution No. 20-26, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPOINTING VICE MAYOR TONY AYALA AS THE CITY’S ALTERNATE TO THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY SANITATION DISTRICT NOS. 2 AND 18.

  Report
   11. PLANNING COMMISSIONER REMOVAL AND APPOINTMENT - Staff direction is requested.
  RESOLUTION

  Report

REPORTS

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 20-23 – ADOPTION OF LIST OF PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ROAD
  MAINTENANCE AND REHABILITATION ACCOUNT FUNDS - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 20-23, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 FUNDED BY SB 1: THE ROAD
  REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017.

  Report

  13. 2020 CONSOLIDATED PLAN AND FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN - Provided for City
  Council information regarding proposed activities for the FY 2020-2021 Annual Action Plan.

  Report

  14. AMENDMENT NO. 1 - COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT TO OPERATE THE NORWALK/SANTA FE
  SPRINGS METROLINK STATION – Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 to the
  Cooperative Agreement between the Cities of Norwalk and Santa Fe Springs to change the terms of
  the agreement making the City of Norwalk fully responsible for the maintenance and improvements and
  recipient of all permit parking revenue at the Metrolink Station parking lot; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Amendment No. 1, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney.

  Report

  15. AMENDMENT NO. 1 - - GROUND LEASE AGREEMENT FOR THE NORWALK/SANTA FE SPRINGS
  METROLINK STATION EXPANSION (PARCEL B) - Staff recommends City Council approve
  Amendment No. 1 to the Ground Lease agreement between the Cities of Norwalk and Santa Fe
  Springs for a fifty year (50) term from December 22, 2016, the original start date, through December
  31, 2066, with an option to extend the term for two (2) additional consecutive periods of ten (10) years
  each in a total amount of $70.00; and authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 1, on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated April 16, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
